prompt: Teams first compare their interface definitions when the assembled modules reach the test rig. Which investment would expose disagreements before the modules are built?

options.text: Reserve a second test-rig slot for the assembled modules.
options.feedback: Another slot can help when teams are waiting for equipment. They would still discover the disagreement after building the modules, when several teams may have to repeat design and integration work.

options.text: Check the two versioned interface definitions whenever either changes.
options.feedback: The teams can settle the disagreement while both designs are still open. The reusable check improves the engineering system and can spare the next variant the same late rework.

options.text: Automate distribution of the integration report after each rig test.
options.feedback: Faster reporting helps teams act on a finding once they have it. The first comparison of the definitions would still come after assembly.

prompt: An automated check finds that both modules declare the same unit. Which decision does that result support?

options.text: Take those revisions to integration and investigate timing under load.
options.feedback: The definitions agree on the unit. A test of the integrated modules can address the separate question of whether the value arrives in time.

options.text: Release the product in every intended operating condition.
options.feedback: The check compared the declared units. Release also depends on how the integrated product behaves under its intended operating conditions.

options.text: Count the check as a measured reduction in total development cost.
options.feedback: A passing check records a technical result. A cost claim needs a measure of the work or rework it actually saved.
